memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You still set yourself against my people and will not let them go. Therefore, at this time tomorrow I will send the worst hailstorm that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded till now." - Exodus 9:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God names it plainly: you still set yourself against my people.

There is a personal dimension to Pharaoh's stubbornness. He is not simply making policy decisions. He has set himself — deliberately, actively — against people God has claimed as His own.

That is a dangerous position, and Scripture treats it seriously. What is done to God's people is taken personally by God. Jesus asked Saul on the Damascus road, why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4), even though Saul had been arresting Christians, not Christ.

This cuts two ways for us. If you are suffering for your faith, you are not suffering alone or unnoticed. Christ counts it as done to Him.

And if we are honest, it should also make us examine how we treat other believers — including those we disagree with, those in other churches, those whose personalities irritate us. God takes His people personally.

Notice, once again, the warning comes first: at this time tomorrow. Twenty-four hours of grace before judgement.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I treating God's people the way God treats them?
2. Where have I set myself against something God has clearly said?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me where I have opposed You or wounded Your people. Give me a heart that yields quickly. Amen.
